subject: Human Evolution
title: Immune System Boost
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Immune System Boost.

hook.text: Some of the immune genes you use to fight infections right now came from Neanderthals, not your sapiens ancestors.

buildup.text: Neanderthals lived in Europe for 300,000 years, evolving defenses against local pathogens.

discovery.text: When sapiens interbred with them, they inherited ready-made immune genes—instant local adaptation.

twist.text: These genes were so useful that natural selection strongly favored them, increasing their frequency over time.

climax.text: Interbreeding wasn't just romance—it was an evolutionary shortcut for colonizing new environments.

punchline.text: Neanderthals vaccinated us through their genes.

quiz.question: How did Neanderthal DNA benefit Homo sapiens' immune systems?
options: Inherited immune genes provided ready-made defenses against local pathogens
